findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py:694-697 and :725-729 build the job dict as {number, kind, head, attempt, reoffer?} with no "refresh". After the retrospective-refresh change, job_id() appends ":f<key>" (lifecycle_workers.py job_id) and post_merge_progress offers keyed jobs. So `winning_claim` and `job_outcomes(...).get(job_id(last))` look up keyless ids. An unexpired claim on a keyed terminal job is not seen by the claim guard. The human-decision text for a retrospective-refresh exhaustion reports outcome "unknown" instead of the last keyed outcome. The remedy still works, because the re-offer raises the sequence and widens the refresh bound, but the safety check and the explanation are weaker than for unkeyed jobs.
findings.summary: The re-offer eligibility check and the decision text do not account for the refresh key that the retrospective-refresh change added to post-merge job ids. This is a gap between that change and the existing re-offer code. It does not block the Requirement outcome.
